summary: Incremental index patcher: pre-plans delete/update/skip for the whole batch before mutating anything, so a parse failure never strips a file's existing state. Its synthetic-edge re-derivation at the end is language-gated — each family only re-runs when a file of its language changed — which is what keeps derived edges alive across edits and also what would silently skip a family driven by a non-source input.

summary: Incremental index patcher: pre-plans delete/update/skip for the whole batch before mutating anything, so a parse failure (null) never strips a file's existing state. A parse that hit the time limit is NOT a failure: it returns a path-only result that is reported via reportParseTimeout and applied as an update, so the edited file loses its symbols until it parses in time. Its synthetic-edge re-derivation at the end is language-gated — each family only re-runs when a file of its language changed.
